title: With non-grouped windows, audio icon shown on all windows sharing a PID and parent program, not just the window actually playing sound
line: With task grouping off, only the browser window that is playing sound shows the audio indicator and volume controls, not every window of the browser.
explanation: The task manager links audio streams to tasks only by process ID, and browsers play the sound of every window from one process, so every window of the browser got the audio indicator, the volume slider in its tooltip and the mute action. The window titles already tell which window is playing: Chrome's MPRIS track and Firefox's stream name (media.name) are the playing tab's title, which is also the window title while that tab is shown. Now, when several top-level windows share the stream's process, the streams are kept only on the window whose title contains the stream name or the playing track; if no window title matches (e.g. the playing tab is in the background), all windows keep them as before. The check reruns when window titles, the task list or the MPRIS players change.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: show the audio indicator only on the playing window

With grouping off, every window of a process got the audio indicator and
volume controls, as streams only carry a PID. When one of these windows
has the stream name or playing track in its title, only that one gets it.

BUG: 375943

media.caption: Master, grouping off: Chrome's quiet window (middle) and playing window (right) both show the audio indicator
Fixed: only the playing window shows it
Master: the quiet window's tooltip has the volume slider of the other window's audio (sweep tester's shot, same setup)
Fixed: no volume slider on the quiet window (the media controls row is fixed separately by bug 455654)

review.text: Using window-title matching against stream names and MPRIS track titles for ungrouped windows sharing a PID is a reasonable Plasma-side direction given the upstream browser limitation, and it handles the basic two-window Chrome case well. However, the current implementation has several concrete bugs: it uses the MPRIS track even when the player is paused (letting a paused window steal the audio badge from another playing window), merges the single MPRIS track into every stream's match list (causing one Firefox window to claim another window's separate stream or hide it), fails to clear audioStreamsMatchedByTitle on early return (leaking active Connections on pinned launchers), and misses onRowsRemoved on mpris2Source.
changes: Only use the MPRIS track when the player is actually playing (e.g. check PlaybackStatus === Mpris.PlaybackStatus.Playing) so a paused media tab cannot steal the audio indicator from another playing window.

Match each stream by stream.name first and only fall back to the playing MPRIS track if stream.name does not match any window (avoiding combining stream.name and track in one array so multi-stream browsers like Firefox do not misattribute a second stream to the MPRIS window).

Reset task.audioStreamsMatchedByTitle = false in the early-return branch of updateAudioStreams() when !pa || !task.isWindow so pinned launchers do not keep Connections enabled after their window closes.
Handle onRowsRemoved in the mpris2Source Connections block so removing an MPRIS player recomputes audioStreams.

Guard model.AppPid > 0 (and skip non-window entries) when collecting otherTitles, and filter tasksModel.onDataChanged to avoid re-running updateAudioStreams() whenever unrelated windows change titles.
